scope: Ammonium perturbations shifted active methanogens from Methanosaeta toward other pathways; this does not establish a universal response direction.
Hydrogenotrophic Methanoculleus became prominent under high ammonium in the tested digesters.
Methanosarcina occupied an intermediate response in the ammonium experiment; genus identity alone does not resolve the pathway in this dataset.
The Methanolinea tarda isolate genome supports hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis and formate utilization.
A cultured representative reduced methanol with hydrogen; neither substrate alone supported methane formation.
Reconstructed genomes support methylated-thiol reduction; activity of the study ASVs is not measured.
Stable-isotope-informed metagenomics identified syntrophic butyrate-degrading populations; exact substrate use remains population dependent.
Proteolytic anaerobic isolates were recovered from a brewery-wastewater UASB reactor.
The oil-well isolate uses amino acids and proteinaceous substrates; application to these ASVs is a hypothesis.
